1.note: Here, **house** means all the people descended from a particular person. It envisions them as if they were one household living together. So the **house of Israel** figuratively means all the people descended from the patriarch Jacob, who was also known as Israel. Alternate translation: [you people of Israel]
The speaker is using the phrase **give ear** to mean “listen to me.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly as in the UST.

Here, **house of the king** means all the people who were considered a part of the king’s court as if they were one household living together. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all you who serve in the king’s court]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **judgment**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [you will be judged]

The speaker is speaking of the leaders trying to get the people to sin as if they were setting a trap or a **snare** to catch animals. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a cause of sin]

The speaker is speaking as if the leaders were a trap or **a net spread** to catch prey. He means that they have trapped the people in sin. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you have schemed to make the people sin at Tabor]

2.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **slaughter**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And the revolters have slaughtered many people]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **reproof**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [but I will rebuke all of them]

3.note: The speaker is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **I know** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that he is the one who knows all about them. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [indeed know Ephraim]

The speaker is using the tribe of **Ephraim**, to represent the people of the northern kingdom of Israel. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [you people of the northern kingdom of Israel]

The expression **is not hidden** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and I see Israel clearly]

The speaker is emphasizing a positive meaning by using a negative word, **not**, together with a mild expression that is the opposite of the intended meaning. If it would be helpful in your language, you could emphasize the positive meaning in a strong way. Alternate translation: [and everything about Israel is fully revealed to me]

The expression **is defiled** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Israel has defiled itself]

4.note: The speaker is speaking of their **deeds** as if they were a living thing that could prevent people from doing something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Because of what they have done, they are not able]

The speaker is speaking as if repenting and worshiping God again were to physically change directions and **return** to him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to repent and worship their God again]

The phrase **a spirit of prostitutions** could mean: (1) the prevailing attitude in Israel was in favor of prostitution. Alternate translation: [an attitude of unfaithfulness] or (2) an evil spirit is causing the people to participate in prostitution. Alternate translation: [an evil spirit promoting prostitution]

5.note: The speaker is speaking of **pride** as if it were a living thing that could **testify** against someone. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And Israel’s pride makes his guilt evident]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **pride**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the proud behavior of]
Here, **his face** represents his presence or himself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [against him]

The speaker is speaking of the people’s moral failure as if they actually **stumble** as they walk. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly as modeled in the UST.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **sin**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [from their sinful actions]

6.note: The speaker is speaking of the people trying to appease Yahweh as if they went to **seek** but could not **find** him. He means that the people will pray and make sacrifices to Yahweh but he will not accept it because of their sin. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly as modeled in the UST.

Yahweh is speaking as if his refusal to accept the people’s worship were his having physically **withdrawn** from them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [He refuses to respond to them]

7.note: The speaker is speaking of the people’s failure to keep their covenant with Yahweh as if it had resulted in their having **borne strange children**, that is, producing a generation that does not belong to him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [their descendants do not belong to Yahweh]

The speaker is speaking as if Yahweh would **devour** the people like a predator consuming its prey. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he will destroy them]

The phrase **their portions** could refer to: (1) the people’s portion of the sacrifice that they offer as modeled in the UST, or (2) it could refer to the portion of the land that Yahweh had allotted to them. Alternate translation: [with their portions of the land]

8.note: A **shofar** is a kind of musical instrument made from a ram’s horn. If your readers would not be familiar with what a **shofar** is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [a ram’s horn]
The speaker is calling the city of Bethel **Beth Aven** as a derogatory wordplay because of all the idol worship there. “Bethel” means “house of God” and “Beth Aven” means “house of evil.”

The speaker is using **After you** as a common expression of the culture to mean “lead the way.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Lead the way, Benjamin]

The speaker is using **Benjamin**, to represent the advance warriors of the southern kingdom. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [warriors of Benjamin]

9.note: If your language does not use abstract noun for the idea of **desolation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a wasteland]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **rebuke**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [being rebuked]

10.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **the movers of a boundary** dishonestly steal land that belongs to others by changing the boundaries, so the leaders or **princes of Judah** have violated what rightfully belongs to others. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [like those who dishonestly steal land that belongs to others]

The speaker is speaking of punishing them as if his anger were a liquid that he could **pour out** like water. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will punish them in my anger]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **wrath**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [my great anger]

11.note: The expression **is oppressed, crushed** use passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I will oppress and crush Ephraim]

The terms **oppressed** and **crushed** mean similar things. The speaker is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [severely oppressed]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **judgment**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in the judging of him]

The speaker is speaking as if Ephraim’s devotion to worthless idols were physically having **walked after** them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he devoted himself to what is worthless]

12.note: The point of this comparison is that just as a **moth** slowly destroys clothing by eating through it, so Yahweh will slowly destroy Ephraim. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [the one who destroys Ephraim just as a moth destroys clothing]

The point of this comparison is that just as **rot** slowly destroys wood by decaying it, so Yahweh will slowly destroy the **house of Judah**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and I will slowly destroy the house of Judah just as rot destroys wood]

Here, **house** means all the people descended from a particular person. It envisions them as if they were one household living together. So **the house of Judah** figuratively means all the people descended from the patriarch Judah, who was also known as Israel. Alternate translation: [to the tribe of Judah]

13.note: The speaker is speaking as if Ephraim’s national weakness were a physical **sickness**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [how weak his nation was]

The speaker is speaking as if Judah’s national suffering were a physical **wound**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [how distressed his people were]

13.q: וַ⁠יֵּ֤לֶךְ אֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ אֶל־אַשּׁ֔וּר וַ⁠יִּשְׁלַ֖ח אֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ יָרֵ֑ב
13.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing since **Yareb** was another name for **Assyria**. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them into a single phrase as in the UST. Another approach would be to connect the phrases with a word other than “and” that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [then Ephraim went to Assyria, indeed, he sent to the king of Yareb]

The speaker is stating the pronoun **he** separately, even though the verb translated as **he is not able** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that the king of Assyria is definitely not the one who can help them. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [But the king of Assyria is certainly not able to heal you]

The word **Yareb** represents the written Hebrew text both here and in 10:6. It may be an alternative name for the country of Assyria that is otherwise unknown. Scholars have proposed, however, that a word that shares most of these letters that means “great” would make better sense and may have been original. You may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [the great king]

14.note: The point of this comparison is that just as a **lion** is powerful and tears apart its prey, so Yahweh will powerfully destroy the people of Ephraim and Judah. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [like a lion that will tear apart both Ephraim and]

The speaker is repeating the pronoun **I** separately two times, even though the verb translated as **I will tear** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that Yahweh himself is the one doing this. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [I, Yahweh, myself will tear and go away]

The speaker is speaking of their enemies attacking them as if Yahweh had allowed a predatory animal to **tear** apart its prey and then **go away** and leave them to themselves. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will allow their enemies to attack them and will leave them undefended]

The speaker is speaking of Yahweh causing their enemies to take them into exile as if they were a predatory animal able to **carry off** its prey. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will allow them to be taken into exile in another land]

15.note: The speaker is speaking as if Yahweh had a physical **place** to which he would **return**, meaning that he will withdraw his presence from the people. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I shall withdraw my presence from them]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **guilt**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [they acknowledge that they have sinned]

Here the speaker is speaking of Yahweh as if he were a person located in a specific place that someone would need to **seek**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and want to be reconciled to me again]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **distress**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [When they are suffering]
Here, **my face** represents Yahweh’s presence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [my presence]
The verb translated as **acknowledge their guilt** could also mean, “bear their guilt.” Alternate translation: [they bear their guilt] or [they have been punished for their guilt]
